raw_response:
I am old now, and I do this the way I have done for many years. On my 8 mu I will still plant cotton. I know cotton, and with only 2 people in the house I cannot manage anything too troublesome. Wheat-maize turns too fast and needs more running around, but cotton I can watch little by little. Last year the well water helped, so this year I will keep some money for irrigation if the spring is dry. I do not read those technical things, I look at the soil, the seedlings, and what other people nearby are doing. If the land looks weak, I put a bit more fertilizer; if money is tight, I do not overdo it. Cotton must not miss the right planting time, and later if there are insects, I will spray, because if bugs get bad the bolls suffer and then all the work is wasted. I will use the usual local seed that people around here can buy, not the expensive fancy kind. I want a steady harvest, not taking big risks.
